lines: +30 carry weight

Inscription Gate: You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there.

Azurite Sight: Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked.

Divine Touch: +2% chance for divine azurite; Each chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome.

Ascendant Rune: +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tier; When a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier".
Perfect Inscription: +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tier; A property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier.

Portal Crate: Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal.

Relic Passage: Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included.

Vacuum Chest: Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects.

Chisel Quarrying: Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before.
Last Touch: Runic crafting can overspend an item's potential while any potential remains; the rest drops to zero.
Runic Vise: +1 capacity when crafting with runes; One more alloy or glyph slot at the Runic Anvil, on top of the anvil's own slots.

lines: A Lord's Brand ascends any piece of equipment to the biome after its boss. Weapons, shields, armour and summoning staves: base damage (in the item's own damage types), durability, block and armour rise to that biome's items of the same kind and slot - nothing goes down; a summoning staff's minion becomes as strong as that biome's creatures. Their workbench upgrades start over at quality 1 and then cost what that biome's reference item costs. Properties, sockets, sigils and implicits stay. Equipment with nothing to compare - rings, belts, amulets, trinkets, utility items, capes without armour, tools - gains only item level, unlocking higher property tiers on future rolls; its properties, implicit effects, base stats, durability and quality remain unchanged. One brand per item, and only upward.
new.name: Ascension

lines: A boss essence ascends a weapon, shield or summoning staff to the biome after its boss. Base damage (in the item's own damage types), durability and block rise to that biome's weapons of the same kind - nothing goes down; a summoning staff's minion becomes as strong as that biome's creatures. Workbench upgrades start over at quality 1 and then cost what that biome's weapon costs. Properties, sockets, sigils and implicits stay. One essence per item, and only upward. Rings and belts can also ascend: only their item level rises, unlocking higher property tiers on future rolls. Their current properties, implicit effects, base stats and quality remain unchanged.
old.name: Ascension

lines: A crossbow construct, set up with the siege hammer by any character. It is a skill, not a building: it costs nothing and can stand anywhere, bound only by the ballista limit. It carries a copy of the crossbow in the siege crossbow cell and shoots real bolts from the bolt magazine. When set up it records the crossbow's own damage and a share of its builder's crossbow, projectile, reload and fire-rate bonuses; changing gear later does not change it. Its durability is its crossbow's and runs out by itself in its lifetime, 12 seconds at base; every shot wears it a little more, at zero it falls, and the hammer repairs it. It shoots only while its builder is near.
new.name: Ballista

lines: Slash damage can inflict bleeding by chance; there is no base chance. Bleeding deals 20% of the slash damage of the hit that inflicted it per second for 4 s, over time and through armour. Each player keeps their own strongest bleed on a target; an equal or stronger one refreshes it.
new.name: Bleeding

lines: Slash damage fills the bleeding gauge. When it fills, bleeding deals 20% of the slash damage of the strongest hit in the build-up per second for 4 s, over time and through armour. Bleeding damage, the damage over time multiplier and duration change it separately. Each player keeps their own strongest bleed on a target; a weaker one does not refresh it.
old.name: Bleeding

lines: Makes matching damage apply an ailment more readily. For burning and shock it enlarges each layer a hit leaves; for bleeding and poison it increases their chance, and its flat form is a flat chance. Chill and armour break still fill a gauge, impale uses an application chance.
new.name: Build-up

lines: Makes matching damage apply an ailment more readily. It does not add a missing damage type, increase ailment damage or extend duration; impale uses an application chance instead of a gauge.
old.name: Build-up

lines: Every fire hit leaves a layer of flammability on the target for 8 s, the larger the more of the target's ailment threshold it dealt; the layers add up to 100%, and each hit ignites with a chance equal to them. Burning deals 25% of the fire damage of the igniting hit per second for 4 s, over time; each player keeps their own strongest burn on a target. Tar makes a target more flammable, wet less and shortens burning; chill stops its damage while it lasts, and its time keeps running.
new.name: Burning

lines: Fire damage fills the burning gauge. When it fills, burning deals 25% of the fire damage of the strongest hit in the build-up per second for 4 s, as fire damage over time. Burning damage and the damage over time multiplier make it stronger, duration makes it last longer. Each player keeps their own strongest burn on a target; a weaker one does not refresh it. Wet shortens it, and chill removes it.
old.name: Burning

lines: A charge empowers your next released weapon attack and is consumed even on a miss. Charges do not stack or expire. A charge source can charge the attack again only after its cooldown: 2 s, a critical hit 1.2 s, counted from the last successful charge. A perfect dodge ignores the cooldown and always charges the attack if a dodge roll charges it for you. Spending a charge does not restart cooldowns, and failed grants do not extend them. All hits and projectiles of the released attack share its charge. Spells can consume it only with Charged Casts. The charge itself grants 25% increased damage; charged-attack nodes add further bonuses.
new.name: Charged attack

lines: A charge empowers your next released weapon attack and is consumed even on a miss. Charges do not stack or expire. A charge source can charge the attack again only after its cooldown: 2 s, a critical hit 0.2 s, counted from the last successful charge. A perfect dodge ignores the cooldown and always charges the attack if a dodge roll charges it for you. Spending a charge does not restart cooldowns, and failed grants do not extend them. All hits and projectiles of the released attack share its charge. Spells can consume it only with Charged Casts. The charge itself grants 25% increased damage; charged-attack nodes add further bonuses.
old.name: Charged attack

lines: A construct is an object a character sets up or creates that acts on its own: ballistas, ice crystals, spores, armour shards, Mountain Bells, and a Steelskaldr's living weapons. Its durability is its health, and it runs out by itself in its lifetime: effect duration lengthens the lifetime and reduced decay slows the loss. At zero a ballista falls and the created ones go off. Living weapons do not decay: their durability is a real item's. A bonus for constructs reaches every construct that has the bonused property.
new.name: Construct

lines: Your attacks cannot damage player-built pieces, including your own. Enemy attacks and natural objects are unaffected. You can still dismantle pieces with the hammer. Carts, ships and siege machines, which the hammer cannot dismantle, can still be broken.
new.name: Careful Builder

lines: Your attacks cannot damage player-built pieces, including your own. Enemy attacks and natural objects are unaffected. You can still dismantle pieces with the hammer.
old.name: Careful Builder

lines: A damaging ailment deals its damage faster: burning, poison or bleeding with 25% increased damage over time speed deals 25% more damage per second and ends sooner, so its total damage stays the same. General rows and rows of the ailment add together.
new.name: Damage over Time Speed

lines: Bow shots deal full damage up to their effective range. Beyond it, damage first decreases gradually, then falls more steeply to a fifth at the far limit. Increased effective range stretches the entire curve. Crossbows have no effective range: they deal full damage at any distance.
new.name: Effective Range

lines: Bow and crossbow shots deal full damage up to their effective range. Beyond it, damage first decreases gradually, then falls more steeply to a fifth at the far limit. Increased effective range stretches the entire curve.
old.name: Effective Range

lines: An elemental damage type whose hits build flammability on the target and can ignite it (burning). Damage from the hit is separate from burning damage over time.
new.name: Fire damage

lines: An elemental damage type that fills the burning gauge. Damage from the hit is separate from burning damage over time.
old.name: Fire damage

lines: Burning and chill live together. While a target is chilled its burning deals no damage, but the burning's time keeps running; once the chill ends, the burning hurts as usual.
new.name: Fire and Frost

lines: Burning and chill cannot coexist. Applying either removes the other.
old.name: Fire and Frost

lines: Frost damage fills the chill gauge. Chill slows movement, weakens over time and stops the damage of burning while it lasts; frost-resistant creatures are protected from the slow.
new.name: Chill

lines: Frost damage fills the chill gauge. Chill slows movement, weakens over time and removes burning; frost-resistant creatures are protected from the slow.
old.name: Chill

lines: Restores a share of health actually removed by a qualifying hit after armour and resistances. Weapon and projectile hits leech only from their physical damage (blunt, slashing, piercing) - the fire, frost, lightning, poison and spirit of an attack restore nothing; spell hits leech from all their damage through spell leech, while indirect damage and resource hits do not qualify.
new.name: Life leech

lines: Restores a share of health actually removed by a qualifying hit after armour and resistances. Weapon and projectile hits use life leech; spell hits use spell leech, while indirect damage and resource hits do not qualify. Each hit starts its own leech that restores 2% of maximum health per second until it has given back its share; all leech together restores at most 20% per second and stops at full health.
old.name: Life leech

lines: An elemental damage type whose hits build conductivity on the target and can shock it. A shocked target takes more damage and builds up stagger faster for a few seconds.
new.name: Lightning damage

lines: An elemental damage type that fills the shock gauge. A shocked target takes more damage and builds up stagger faster for a few seconds.
old.name: Lightning damage

lines: Tags: skill, construct, area, damage, build-up.

Hold your alternative attack to see the place and the eitr it will reserve, release to call the Bell: it falls from the sky on the ground in front of you, up to 14 m away, and its landing hurts nobody. A bad spot or too little eitr refuses the call and costs nothing.

Cooldown 8 s, the same for every sceptre of this character. It stands 20 s (base 20), its wave reaches 4 m (base 4), you keep up to 1: a new Bell at the limit replaces your oldest. Each Bell reserves 35% of maximum eitr until it leaves, you die or the sceptre comes off.

Every weapon hit on it, yours or an ally's, shots included, rings it: a wave passes 40-60% of that hit to each enemy around, damage and every build-up alike. Crit, leech and kills belong to the one who struck; defence, resistances and conditions are the enemy's own. Enemy hits, damage over time and other waves do not ring it. Striking it is not hitting an enemy: the blow itself gives no on-hit reward.

Scales with: area of effect (it grows the area, so the radius grows as its square root), effect duration, construct and Bell rows, eitr reservation efficiency; the wave with the damage, build-up and area damage of the one who struck.
new.name: Mountain Bell

lines: A socket beyond the item's socket limit, opened by the Glyph of the Void. It takes what an ordinary socket takes and stays through punches, reforging and repairs.
new.name: Phantom socket

lines: A melee attack hit can cause a phantom strike against a random nearby enemy, including the original target. Only the weapon's own blow counts: projectiles, spells and area blows such as a sceptre's Smite lightning do not. It deals 24% of the original hit's calculated damage before the target's defences. Damage modifiers are not applied again, and it does not roll a new critical strike or trigger on-hit effects. Every full 100% chance guarantees one phantom strike; the remainder rolls for one more. Only Endless Apparition allows phantom strikes to trigger further phantom strikes.
new.name: Phantom Strikes

lines: A melee attack hit can cause a phantom strike against a random nearby enemy, including the original target. Only the weapon's own blow counts: projectiles, spells and area blows such as a sceptre's Smite lightning do not. It deals 24% of the original hit's calculated damage before the target's defences. Damage modifiers are not applied again, and it does not trigger on-hit effects. It rolls its own critical strike with the critical strike chance and damage of the original hit plus those for phantom strikes. It builds up no ailments, and it builds up half the stagger of the original hit, raised by stagger build-up for phantom strikes. Every full 100% chance guarantees one phantom strike; the remainder rolls for one more. Only Endless Apparition allows phantom strikes to trigger further phantom strikes.
old.name: Phantom Strikes

lines: Poison damage can poison by chance; there is no base chance, and every full 100% of chance adds a certain poison. Each poison deals 15% of the poison damage of its hit per second for 4 s on its own timer; a player keeps up to 3 on a target, the poison limit raises that, and a new one replaces the weakest if stronger. Poison is separate from elemental damage.
new.name: Poison

lines: Poison damage fills the poison gauge. When it fills, poison deals 15% of the poison damage of the strongest hit in the build-up per second for 4 s. Each player can keep up to 3 poisons on a target at once, and a poison limit raises that; a new poison on a full set replaces the weakest, if it is stronger. Poison damage and the damage over time multiplier make it stronger. Poison is separate from elemental damage.
old.name: Poison

lines: A damage type that can poison by chance. It is separate from elemental damage and from poison damage over time.
new.name: Poison damage

lines: A damage type that fills the poison gauge. It is separate from elemental damage and from poison damage over time.
old.name: Poison damage

lines: An item's budget for runic crafting: 100 on every ordinary piece of equipment. Each runic action costs 15 plus the costs of its alloys and glyphs; a critical craft costs half. At zero the item still works, but runic crafting is closed. Repairs and workbench upgrades do not restore it.
new.name: Potential

lines: Items: Common items have no random affixes. Magic items have 1–2 affixes: at most 1 prefix and 1 suffix. Rare items have 3–6 affixes: at most 3 prefixes and 3 suffixes. Implicit properties do not count towards these limits. Unique and Legendary items have their own properties and rules. Creatures: no stars means Common, 1–2 stars Magic, 3–4 Rare, and 5 or more Unique. Each star grants a modifier and increases health, damage and loot.
new.name: Rarity

lines: Items: Common items have no random affixes. Magic items have 1–2 affixes: at most 1 prefix and 1 suffix. Rare items have 3–4 affixes: at most 2 prefixes and 2 suffixes. Implicit properties do not count towards these limits. Unique and Legendary items have their own properties and rules. Creatures: no stars means Common, 1–2 stars Magic, 3–4 Rare, and 5 or more Unique. Each star grants a modifier and increases health, damage and loot.
old.name: Rarity

lines: A crafting station for alloys and glyphs. Its stock keeps one slot per kind with no limit; upgrades open up to four shared slots, and a Runecarver adds one more of their own. Forging makes the item rare with two prefixes and two suffixes; alloys make the properties of their theme more likely.
new.name: Runic Anvil

lines: Every lightning hit leaves a layer of conductivity on the target for 8 s, and each hit shocks with a chance equal to all layers, up to 100%. A shocked target takes 20% more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster for 3 s; shock effect raises this, up to 50%. Only the strongest shock on a target acts, and it deals no damage itself.
new.name: Shock

lines: Lightning damage fills the shock gauge. When it fills, the target is shocked for 3 s: it takes more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster, both by the shock's strength. Strength depends on the lightning damage of the strongest hit in the build-up, before the target's defences, compared with the target's ailment threshold: a hit of 1% of it shocks for about 8%. Below 5% there is no shock, and it never goes above 50%. Shock effect makes it stronger, ailment duration makes it last longer. Only the strongest shock on a target acts, and a weaker one does not refresh it. Shock is not a stun and deals no damage itself.
old.name: Shock

lines: A physical damage type that can inflict bleeding by chance. Bleeding needs both slash damage and a bleeding chance; there is no base chance.
new.name: Slash damage

lines: A physical damage type that fills the bleeding gauge. Bleeding requires slash damage, not just a build-up bonus.
old.name: Slash damage

lines: Bombs or any thrown ammunition, including thrown meads
new.name: Ammunition

lines: Each unit of ordinary copper, tin, scrap, silver or flametal mined may come with one unusual ore of the same metal beside it, at a small chance. The unusual ore smelts into a themed alloy for the Runic Anvil.
new.name: Unusual ore
